perspective:
**Brandon’s available information:**

- I am an insurance agent. I met Benjamin, an entrepreneur, in a professional setting because he wanted business insurance advice. I knew he had limited formal education, so I was concerned about explaining complex insurance details clearly.
- In our first meeting, I heard Benjamin say he wanted everything covered but some terms were new. I explained comprehensive coverage, liability insurance as a safety net, a slip-and-fall example, and asset protection covering inventory/equipment. Benjamin said it made sense, asked about assets, and thanked me for breaking it down.
- In a later meeting, based on our previous interactions, I revised my belief that Benjamin could understand detailed information. I felt more confident and planned to discuss more complex details. I explained business interruption insurance and property insurance. Benjamin said he had been reading up, found business interruption crucial, and called comprehensive coverage reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, I worried I was too detail-focused and wanted to keep things engaging. Benjamin said he appreciates my thoroughness but also enjoys lighter moments. I told a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds; Benjamin found it fascinating. I connected it to assessing risks for his business, and he agreed it was less unusual but equally important.
- After that, pleased by Benjamin’s positive response, I decided to offer more value beyond insurance. I asked if he had considered strategic investments to lower premiums; he had not but liked the idea. I suggested upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin called it a win-win and agreed to explore it further.
- Later, encouraged by our rapport and what I saw as mutual benefit, I felt optimistic about proposing a joint venture. I proposed co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, called it groundbreaking, said combining our expertise could set us apart, and agreed to draft initial plans.
